newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ex-top cop to testify in Mexico body-snatching case.
newsitem.headline: Ex-top cop to testify in Mexico body-snatching case.

text.p: Mexico's former attorney general said on Tuesday he would appear before judicial authorities to give evidence on his actions in office --including a bizarre case involving a skeleton, a witch and allegations of body snatching and bribery.
Antonio Lozano Gracia, who was fired by President Ernesto Zedillo on Dec. 2, said he would answer "each and every question" officials asked him.
Lozano, a legislator for the conservative National Action Party (PAN) and until his firing the only opposition member of Zedillo's Cabinet, said he had been summoned to appear on Thursday.
"I will be there on time," Lozano said in a statement.
He has not been charged with any wrong-doing.

Authorities were likely to ask him about a case involving allegedly illegal payments to witnesses and other bizarre aspects of the probe into the Sept. 28, 1994, assassination of ruling party leader Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu.

Lozano said last year that a skeleton dug up at a ranch used by former President Carlos Salinas' brother Raul was likely that of a missing legislator believed to have been killed because of his part in the Ruiz murder.
Raul Salinas is in jail on charges of planning the Ruiz murder and authorities were trying to pin the suspected murder of the legislator on him too.

The skeleton turned out to have been planted by a witch and soothsayer who was helping Lozano's top investigator in the case. DNA testing showed it was not the missing man, but a relative of the witch's whose body she and other relatives had stolen from a cemetery and reburied at the ranch.

The witch has been charged with body snatching and grave robbing while the investigator, Pablo Chapa Bezanilla, is on the run from justice over allegations that he paid $450,000 dollars to witnesses in the case.
Lozano has said that the payments were brought to the attention of Zedillo, but spokesmen for the president say he never authorised them.
